newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds, futures climb but resistance caps gains.
newsitem.headline: Bunds, futures climb but resistance caps gains.

text.p: German Bund futures, defying some dealers' forecasts, vaulted across the key 97.00 level in late Wednesday trading, managing to shrug off the effects from a slightly weaker U.S. market.
"Technically the German market looks good, a bit better than we expected," said one dealer, explaining why the German market had managed to fare better than the U.S. market.
Bunds were trading up 28 basis points at 97.09, just below the day's high of 97.11 and far above the low of 96.78.
But dealers also said the market was still lacking the necessary momentum to move above resistance at 97.12.
Meanwhile U.S. Treasuries were lower as the market remained worried that rising inflationary pressures could soon force the U.S. central bank to raise interest rates in the near future.

Dealers said that staring at U.S. indicators and officials' comments would only increase in the run-up to the Fed's late September meeting when some officials are fearing the central bank will have little choice but to raise short-term interest rates.
So as the market anticipates Thursday's U.S. PPI data, dealers expect the German market will trade in a relatively narrow range.
"We could move between 96.80 and today's highs while waiting for the U.S. numbers to come out tomorrow," one dealer said.
Should the Bund futures test support and break it, dealers said a move to 96.50 could be seen relatively quickly.
But dealers generally said that most activity would occur Thursday afternoon, dictated largely by the U.S. numbers are and how the U.S. market will react to them.
